properties.label: Password

properties.label: ClientID
properties.description: The client-id used when connecting to MQTT.

properties.label: ImportProfiles
properties.description: Custom topic shapes for the MQTT Import page, for publishers with no built-in profile.

properties.label: Name
properties.description: Name shown in the MQTT Import source list.

properties.label: Filter
properties.description: Subscription filter to browse, e.g. 'tele/#'. Narrow it: a broker's ACL may refuse '#'.

properties.label: Pattern
properties.description: Topic shape, with {device} and {measure} marking the parts to capture and '+' matching any single segment. e.g. 'tele/{device}/SENSOR/{measure}'.

properties.label: JsonField
properties.description: Field holding the value when the payload is JSON — dotted for nesting. Leave blank when the payload is the bare number.

properties.label: Metrics
properties.description: Captured {measure} -> the metric it supplies. Measures not listed are ignored.

properties.label: ParentTopic
properties.description: The parent topic for MQTT messages.

properties.label: Connection
properties.description: Connection details for MQTT Broker

properties.label: Connection Scheme
properties.description: How to reach the broker: mqtt (plain TCP), mqtts (TLS), ws (WebSocket) or wss (WebSocket over TLS). Leave unset to infer from the port.

properties.label: Host
properties.description: Hostname or IP to connect to.

properties.label: Port
properties.description: The port to connect to.

properties.label: Connection Timeout
properties.description: Default connection timeout.

properties.label: Validate Certificate
properties.description: Enables certificate validation

properties.label: PublishTimeoutSeconds
properties.description: Seconds to wait for the broker to acknowledge a publish before abandoning it and failing the pass loudly. Stops one unacknowledged message from silently wedging publishing altogether.

properties.label: KeepAlive
properties.description: The keepalive interval for the MQTT connection in seconds.

properties.label: Last Will / Availability
properties.description: Publish a Last-Will message and set an availability topic on entities, so Home Assistant marks them unavailable immediately when the bridge disconnects. When off, entities instead rely on HomeAssistant.SensorExpireAfterSeconds (expire_after) to go unavailable.

properties.label: Message Timestamp
properties.description: Carry the time a measurement was read. 'None' (default) publishes exactly as before. 'UserProperty' adds an MQTT v5 'timestamp' property and leaves the payload alone — verify it against your broker first, since a broker or client that mishandles user properties on PUBLISH can drop the connection. 'Payload' publishes {"value": …, "timestamp": …} instead of a bare value (Home Assistant discovery adapts automatically).

description: PDU instances to bridge, keyed by instance name.

properties.description: Connection details for PDU

properties.label: Host
properties.description: Hostname or IP to connect to.

properties.label: Credentials
properties.description: PDU login used for write actions (outlet control). Can also be supplied via RPDU2MQTT_PDU_USERNAME / RPDU2MQTT_PDU_PASSWORD.

properties.description: Username to log in as

properties.label: Password

properties.label: Poll Interval (seconds)
properties.description: How often (seconds) to poll the PDU and publish readings.

properties.label: Enable Write Actions
properties.description: Allow the bridge to make changes on the PDU (e.g. toggle outlets). When off, no switches or other write controls are exposed to Home Assistant. Requires PDU credentials.

properties.label: Remap Model column
properties.description: Replace each outlet/group's Model (shown in the Home Assistant device info) with contextual text (e.g. parent PDU + name) instead of the PDU's hardware model.

properties.label: Remap Manufacturer column
properties.description: Replace each entity's Manufacturer (shown in Home Assistant) with the entity type (Outlet, Group, etc.) instead of the hardware manufacturer.

properties.label: DiscoveryEnabled
properties.description: Indicates whether Home Assistant discovery is enabled.

properties.label: DiscoveryTopic
properties.description: The discovery topic for Home Assistant.

properties.label: DiscoveryInterval
properties.description: How often (seconds) to republish discovery. 0 = run once at startup until restarted.

properties.label: DiscoveryRetain
properties.description: Whether discovery messages are retained on the broker.

properties.label: SensorExpireAfterSeconds
properties.description: expire_after (seconds) applied to sensors; after this long without an update Home Assistant marks them unavailable.

properties.label: GroupMemberNameTemplate
properties.description: Name template for a group's mirrored member switches. Placeholders: {device}, {outlet}, {number}, {group}.

properties.label: GroupMemberObjectIdTemplate
properties.description: Stable entity/object_id template for a group's mirrored member switches. Placeholders: {serial}, {number}, {device}, {group}.

properties.label: EnergyDashboard
properties.description: Auto-configure Home Assistant's Energy Dashboard 'devices' (with upstream relationships) from the energy-flow hierarchy, via HA's WebSocket API.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Sync the energy-flow hierarchy into HA's Energy Dashboard via its API. Requires Url + a long-lived access token.

properties.label: NodeTags
properties.description: Limit the Energy Dashboard sync to nodes with particular tags. Empty syncs every node. Filtering changes only what is sent — never a value, and never any other destination.

properties.label: Include
properties.description: Only send nodes carrying at least one of these tags. Empty sends every node.

properties.label: Exclude
properties.description: Never send nodes carrying any of these tags. Takes precedence over Include.

properties.label: Url
properties.description: Home Assistant base URL, e.g. http://homeassistant.local:8123 .

properties.label: Token
properties.description: Home Assistant long-lived access token (or set RPDU2MQTT_HASS_TOKEN).

properties.label: EnergyMeasurementType
properties.description: Measurement type holding each entity's cumulative energy (kWh) — used to find the Energy Dashboard stat for each tier.

properties.label: ExcludeDeviceKinds
properties.description: Node kinds to leave OUT of the Energy Dashboard's individual-devices list (they're sources/storage/pass-through, shown as the dashboard's grid/solar/battery sources instead). Default: grid, solar, battery, inverter. Empty list = export every tier.

properties.label: Exporter
properties.description: Expose a /metrics endpoint for Prometheus to scrape.

properties.label: NodeTags
properties.description: Limit the energy-flow metrics to nodes with particular tags. Empty exposes every node. Filtering changes only what is scraped — never a value, and never any other destination.

properties.label: Include
properties.description: Only send nodes carrying at least one of these tags. Empty sends every node.

properties.label: Exclude
properties.description: Never send nodes carrying any of these tags. Takes precedence over Include.

properties.label: Port
properties.description: Port the /metrics endpoint listens on (Exporter).

properties.label: MetricNameTemplate
properties.description: Template for Prometheus metric names. Placeholders: {type}, {device}, {source} (a.k.a. {outlet}), {units}. e.g. 'rpdu2mqtt_{type}' -> rpdu2mqtt_realpower; 'pdu_{device}_{type}' -> pdu_rack_pdu_1_realpower. (device/source/units are also emitted as labels.)

properties.label: Labels
properties.description: Labels attached to every exported metric. Available: device, device_name (the device's display name), source, name (the outlet/entity's display name), number, type, type_name (the measurement said in English, e.g. 'Real Power'), units, instance (PDU instance key), hierarchy (the energy-flow tier feeding it). Changing this changes every metric's label set.

properties.label: Pushgateway
properties.description: Push metrics to a Prometheus Pushgateway.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Push metrics to a Pushgateway.

properties.label: Url
properties.description: Pushgateway endpoint, e.g. http://pushgateway:9091/metrics.

properties.label: Job
properties.description: The 'job' label applied to pushed metrics.

properties.label: IntervalSeconds
properties.description: How often to push, in seconds. Falls back to the PDU poll interval when 0.

properties.label: ValueFallback
properties.description: Let the history backend supply a value for any node nothing live is reporting. Off by default: a stored value is older than a live one, and for a node whose source has stopped it replaces an honest "no data" with a figure that looks current.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Let the Flow and Energy pages show a past moment, read from Prometheus or EmonCMS.

properties.label: Provider
properties.description: Which backend to read from: 'prometheus' or 'emoncms'.

properties.label: PrometheusUrl
properties.description: Prometheus base URL to query, e.g. http://prometheus:9090 . This is the server that scrapes this bridge, not the /metrics endpoint it exposes.

properties.label: ToleranceSeconds
properties.description: How far either side of the requested moment to look for a sample, in seconds. A scrape or feed interval longer than this returns nothing rather than a value from a different time.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Push measurements to an EmonCMS server.

properties.label: Transport
properties.description: How to deliver measurements: Http (input/post API) or Mqtt (publish to EmonCMS's MQTT input on the same broker).

properties.label: Url
properties.description: Base URL of the EmonCMS server, e.g. http://emoncms.example.com. (Http transport.)

properties.label: ApiKey
properties.description: EmonCMS write API key (or set RPDU2MQTT_EMONCMS_APIKEY). (Http transport.)

properties.label: Node
properties.description: EmonCMS input node name.

properties.label: Path
properties.description: API path (relative to Url) that measurements are posted to. (Http transport.)

properties.label: InputNameTemplate
properties.description: Template for EmonCMS input keys. Placeholders: {device}, {source} (object-id form), {name} (formatted display name), {number} (outlet number), {type}, {units}. e.g. '{device}_{source}_{type}' -> rack_pdu_1_dell_md1200_realpower. Leave blank to use the full raw identifier.

properties.label: ExportFlowNodes
properties.description: Also send each energy-flow node (panels, inverters, batteries, the grid) as its own input, not just the PDU measurements. This is what gives those nodes history to read back.

properties.label: NodeTags
properties.description: Limit the exported energy-flow nodes to particular tags. Empty sends every node. Filtering changes only what is sent — never a value, and never any other destination.

properties.label: Include
properties.description: Only send nodes carrying at least one of these tags. Empty sends every node.

properties.label: Exclude
properties.description: Never send nodes carrying any of these tags. Takes precedence over Include.

properties.label: FlowInputNameTemplate
properties.description: Template for an energy-flow node's EmonCMS input key. Placeholders: {node} (its id), {label}, {kind}, {metric}, {units}. e.g. '{node}_{metric}' -> solar_realpower. The history reader looks feeds up by this name.

properties.label: MqttBaseTopic
properties.description: Base MQTT topic for EmonCMS's MQTT input (the {base} placeholder of MqttTopicTemplate). (Mqtt transport.)

properties.label: MqttTopicTemplate
properties.description: Template for the EmonCMS MQTT topic each JSON payload is published to. Placeholders: {base} (MqttBaseTopic), {node}, {device} (the PDU's name). Including {device} splits the export so each PDU publishes to its own topic instead of one combined payload, e.g. '{base}/{node}/{device}'. (Mqtt transport.)

properties.label: Feeds
properties.description: Automatically create and maintain EmonCMS feeds from the exported inputs. (Http transport; needs a read/write API key.)

properties.label: AutoConfigure
properties.description: Create and maintain EmonCMS feeds from the exported inputs (takes effect without a restart).

properties.label: Types
properties.description: The supported measurement types. Each says whether it gets a feed, how that feed is named and stored, and whether EmonCMS derives it.

properties.label: Type
properties.description: The measurement type this applies to.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Build and maintain a feed for this type.

properties.label: Calculation
properties.description: Who works this type out. Prefer local uses this bridge's reading where it has one and an EmonCMS process otherwise; prefer EmonCMS reverses that — energy integrated from power, power from an energy counter, the daily total from either. The Force options use only that one and leave the feed unwritten when it cannot answer. Only power, energy and daily energy can be derived; every other type is recorded as it arrives.

properties.label: Prefix
properties.description: Text placed before the feed name. Blank by default. Placeholders: {device}, {source}, {name}, {number}, {type}, {units}.

properties.label: Suffix
properties.description: Text placed after the feed name, which is where the type appears. Placeholders: {device}, {source}, {name}, {number}, {type}, {units}.

properties.label: Units
properties.description: The unit this feed is stored in.

properties.label: Engine
properties.description: Feed storage engine for this type. Blank inherits Feeds.Engine. PHPFina = fixed-interval, PHPTimeSeries = variable, MySQL = MySQL storage.

properties.label: IntervalSeconds
properties.description: Sample interval in seconds for this type's feed.

properties.label: Engine
properties.description: Default feed storage engine, for types that don't set their own. PHPFina = fixed-interval time series, PHPTimeSeries = variable interval, MySQL = MySQL storage (no phpfina files).

properties.label: IntervalSeconds
properties.description: Default sample interval in seconds for a fixed-interval feed, for types that don't set their own.

properties.label: Tag
properties.description: The EmonCMS tag (group) new feeds are filed under. Blank uses the input node name.

properties.label: StorageNameTemplate
properties.description: Template for the storage-feed name, without the type — each type appends its own suffix. Use only stable placeholders ({device}, {source}, {number}) so the name never changes on a rename. Placeholders: {device}, {source}, {name}, {number}, {units}.

properties.label: Virtual
properties.description: Optionally create friendly-named virtual feeds that source from the stable storage feeds — so dashboards get nice names while the underlying feeds stay idempotent.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Create a friendly-named virtual feed for each storage feed, sourced from it (source_feed process).

properties.label: NameTemplate
properties.description: Template for the friendly virtual-feed name. {name} is the source's display name, so these can change freely without touching the stable storage feeds. Placeholders: {device}, {source}, {name}, {number}, {type}, {units}.

properties.label: Tag
properties.description: The EmonCMS tag (group/node) virtual feeds are filed under — set this to keep the friendly virtual feeds separate from the storage feeds. Blank uses the main Feeds tag.

properties.label: Source
properties.description: Read EmonCMS feeds back as live values for energy-flow nodes (bind a node's source with Type 'emoncms').

properties.label: PollIntervalSeconds
properties.description: How often to read the bound feeds' current values, in seconds. One request per poll however many feeds are bound.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Enable the embedded configuration web GUI.
properties.notEditableReason: Turning the GUI off from inside the GUI would lock you out of the only place you could turn it back on. Set it where the deployment is defined — the Helm values, the container environment, or config.yaml.

properties.label: ShowProjectLink
properties.description: Show a link to the project's GitHub page in the GUI. Turn off for a cleaner look on a shared screen.

properties.label: Authentication
properties.description: How users authenticate to the GUI: Basic (username/password), Oidc (SSO), or None (no login).

properties.label: Port
properties.description: Port the configuration GUI listens on.

properties.label: Username
properties.description: Username required to access the GUI (HTTP Basic auth).

properties.label: Password
properties.description: Password required to access the GUI (HTTP Basic auth). Required unless Oidc is enabled.

properties.label: Oidc
properties.description: OpenID Connect (SSO) settings (used when AuthType is Oidc).

properties.label: Authority
properties.description: OIDC authority / issuer URL (e.g. https://keycloak.example.com/realms/home).

properties.label: ClientId
properties.description: OIDC client ID registered with your identity provider.

properties.label: ClientSecret
properties.description: OIDC client secret. Prefer the RPDU2MQTT_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET env var (or *_FILE secret).

properties.label: Scopes
properties.description: Space-separated scopes to request.

properties.label: CallbackPath
properties.description: Redirect/callback path registered with the identity provider.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Expose HTTP health-check endpoints: /healthz (liveness) and /readyz (readiness).

properties.label: Port
properties.description: Port the health-check endpoints listen on.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Expose a read-only REST API (/api/v1/*) with OpenAPI + Scalar docs on its own port. Place it on a trusted network — it is unauthenticated, like the health endpoints.

properties.label: Port
properties.description: Port the REST API + docs listen on.

properties.label: ApiKey
properties.description: Optional API key enabling the write/control endpoints (or set RPDU2MQTT_API_KEY). When unset, the API is read-only; when set, control requests must send a matching 'X-Api-Key' header. Reads stay open (trusted-network).

label: EnergyFlow
description: Virtual upstream nodes (breakers, transfer switches, a “Total”) and their feeder wiring for the energy-flow hierarchy. Edited visually on the Flow tab.

properties.label: Aggregation
properties.description: Accumulate energy (kWh) from the power readings, for nodes that report power but not energy.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Derive energy (kWh) by integrating each node's power over time. A real energy source on a node always takes precedence.

properties.label: SampleIntervalSeconds
properties.description: How often to sample power, in seconds. Shorter samples track a spiky load more closely.

properties.label: MaxGapSeconds
properties.description: Longest gap between samples that still counts, in seconds. A longer gap is recorded as unmeasured rather than guessed.

properties.label: TrackPeriods
properties.description: Track a daily energy total per node and outlet, so the flow diagram compares figures that all start at the same moment. Lifetime totals are unaffected.

properties.label: PeriodTimeZone
properties.description: IANA time zone the daily total rolls over in, e.g. "America/Chicago". Blank uses the host's local time zone — which in a container is usually UTC.

properties.label: PeriodStartHour
properties.description: Hour of the day the daily total rolls over, in the period time zone. 0 = midnight.

properties.label: Nodes
properties.description: Custom upstream flow nodes (breakers, transfer-switch outputs, Total, ...), keyed by a stable id.

properties.label: Id
properties.description: Stable unique id used to wire parents/children.

properties.label: Label
properties.description: Human-readable label shown in the flow diagram.

properties.label: Kind
properties.description: What this node represents: 'node' (generic), 'panel', 'inverter', 'battery', 'solar', 'grid', or 'load'. Drives styling and the fields the editor offers.

properties.label: Value
properties.description: Optional fixed value for a leaf node. Used only when no live source has reported for it.

properties.label: Max
properties.description: Full-scale value for this node's gauge, in the metric's canonical unit (W for power). For example a PV array's peak output. Leave blank to show the plain reading instead — no ceiling is ever guessed.

properties.label: Tags
properties.description: Free-form tags for filtering the diagram and the energy views — e.g. 'critical', 'rack-1', 'upstairs'. A tag never changes a reading, only what a view shows.

properties.label: StorageKwh
properties.description: For a battery node: usable storage capacity in kWh (display metadata; optional).

properties.label: Mode
properties.description: How to value this node when it has no direct measurement: 'auto' (aggregate children; carries unmet demand only when it is the single path into a node — never splits a load between several unmeasured feeders), 'static' (a fixed leaf at Value), 'residual' (the designated absorber of what its target still needs — this is how you say where unaccounted power comes from), 'untracked' (show a measured parent's unaccounted consumption), or 'none' (never inferred). A live source always wins.

properties.label: Sources
properties.description: Live value bindings for this node, one per metric. Each binds a metric to an external source (Type 'mqtt' today). Supersedes Value.

properties.label: Type
properties.description: Where this value comes from: 'mqtt' (subscribe to a broker topic), 'modbus' (read a register from a Modbus TCP connection), 'emoncms' (read an EmonCMS feed's current value), 'homeassistant' (read an entity's state), or 'derived' (work it out from this node's other readings — current as power ÷ voltage, for a meter that reports watts and volts but no amps).

properties.label: Metric
properties.description: Which measurement this source supplies (the flow is rolled up per metric): realpower = power, apparentpower, energy, current, voltage, frequency, powerfactor, or soc (battery state of charge %, shown on the Energy tile — not rolled up).

properties.label: Accumulation
properties.description: Whether this counter runs forever or restarts each day: 'lifetime' (default — a cumulative total whose rise is measured) or 'period' (the device resets it daily, so the reading already is today's total). Only meaningful for energy. Check the topic before choosing: a publisher can offer both kinds, and firmware changes which. A daily counter tagged 'lifetime' is read as a meter running backwards every midnight and stops being published; a lifetime counter tagged 'period' is republished every poll as if that whole total were today's.

properties.label: Direction
properties.description: Which way energy flows for this source, relative to the node: 'out' (default — battery discharge, grid import, solar production), 'in' (battery charge, grid export), or 'split' — one signed value fanned into both directions, positive as out and the magnitude of negative as in (for a single ± power/current topic or register). Only meaningful for directional metrics (realpower, apparentpower, current, energy); ignored for voltage/frequency/powerfactor/soc.

properties.label: Unit
properties.description: Unit the source publishes in (e.g. kW, Wh, mV). Converted to the metric's canonical unit (W, kWh, V, …) on ingest. Blank = already canonical.

properties.label: Topic
properties.description: For Type 'mqtt': the topic carrying this value, e.g. 'solar_assistant/inverter_1/pv_power/state'. Subscribed on the configured broker.

properties.label: JsonField
properties.description: For JSON payloads, the field to read (dotted for nesting, e.g. 'battery.power'). Blank = the whole payload is the number.

properties.label: Scale
properties.description: Multiplier applied to the received value — for unit conversion, e.g. 0.001 to turn W into kW, or -1 to flip a sign convention.

properties.label: StaleAfterSeconds
properties.description: Ignore the last value once it is this old, so a dead publisher stops silently propping up the flow. 0 disables the check (value never expires).

properties.label: Connection
properties.description: For Type 'modbus': the id of the Modbus connection (from the Modbus section) to read from.

properties.label: Register
properties.description: For Type 'modbus': the register address to read (0-based).

properties.label: RegisterType
properties.description: For Type 'modbus': which register bank — 'holding' (function 3) or 'input' (function 4).

properties.label: DataType
properties.description: For Type 'modbus': how to decode the register(s) — uint16, int16, uint32, int32, or float32.

properties.label: WordOrder
properties.description: For Type 'modbus' 32-bit values: word order — 'big' (ABCD, high word first) or 'little' (CDAB, word-swapped).

properties.label: Feed
properties.description: For Type 'emoncms': the feed to read — its numeric id (e.g. 945), or its name (e.g. '1_power'). Qualify a name with its tag as 'tag/name' when the same name exists under several tags.

properties.label: Settings
properties.description: Extra settings for a plugin-supplied source type. The built-in mqtt and modbus types use the fields above instead.

properties.label: Mqtt
properties.description: Deprecated: use Sources. Legacy MQTT bindings (implicitly Type 'mqtt'); still honored for back-compat.

properties.label: Type
properties.description: Where this value comes from: 'mqtt' (subscribe to a broker topic), 'modbus' (read a register from a Modbus TCP connection), 'emoncms' (read an EmonCMS feed's current value), 'homeassistant' (read an entity's state), or 'derived' (work it out from this node's other readings — current as power ÷ voltage, for a meter that reports watts and volts but no amps).

properties.label: Metric
properties.description: Which measurement this source supplies (the flow is rolled up per metric): realpower = power, apparentpower, energy, current, voltage, frequency, powerfactor, or soc (battery state of charge %, shown on the Energy tile — not rolled up).

properties.label: Accumulation
properties.description: Whether this counter runs forever or restarts each day: 'lifetime' (default — a cumulative total whose rise is measured) or 'period' (the device resets it daily, so the reading already is today's total). Only meaningful for energy. Check the topic before choosing: a publisher can offer both kinds, and firmware changes which. A daily counter tagged 'lifetime' is read as a meter running backwards every midnight and stops being published; a lifetime counter tagged 'period' is republished every poll as if that whole total were today's.

properties.label: Direction
properties.description: Which way energy flows for this source, relative to the node: 'out' (default — battery discharge, grid import, solar production), 'in' (battery charge, grid export), or 'split' — one signed value fanned into both directions, positive as out and the magnitude of negative as in (for a single ± power/current topic or register). Only meaningful for directional metrics (realpower, apparentpower, current, energy); ignored for voltage/frequency/powerfactor/soc.

properties.label: Unit
properties.description: Unit the source publishes in (e.g. kW, Wh, mV). Converted to the metric's canonical unit (W, kWh, V, …) on ingest. Blank = already canonical.

properties.label: Topic
properties.description: For Type 'mqtt': the topic carrying this value, e.g. 'solar_assistant/inverter_1/pv_power/state'. Subscribed on the configured broker.

properties.label: JsonField
properties.description: For JSON payloads, the field to read (dotted for nesting, e.g. 'battery.power'). Blank = the whole payload is the number.

properties.label: Scale
properties.description: Multiplier applied to the received value — for unit conversion, e.g. 0.001 to turn W into kW, or -1 to flip a sign convention.

properties.label: StaleAfterSeconds
properties.description: Ignore the last value once it is this old, so a dead publisher stops silently propping up the flow. 0 disables the check (value never expires).

properties.label: Connection
properties.description: For Type 'modbus': the id of the Modbus connection (from the Modbus section) to read from.

properties.label: Register
properties.description: For Type 'modbus': the register address to read (0-based).

properties.label: RegisterType
properties.description: For Type 'modbus': which register bank — 'holding' (function 3) or 'input' (function 4).

properties.label: DataType
properties.description: For Type 'modbus': how to decode the register(s) — uint16, int16, uint32, int32, or float32.

properties.label: WordOrder
properties.description: For Type 'modbus' 32-bit values: word order — 'big' (ABCD, high word first) or 'little' (CDAB, word-swapped).

properties.label: Feed
properties.description: For Type 'emoncms': the feed to read — its numeric id (e.g. 945), or its name (e.g. '1_power'). Qualify a name with its tag as 'tag/name' when the same name exists under several tags.

properties.label: Settings
properties.description: Extra settings for a plugin-supplied source type. The built-in mqtt and modbus types use the fields above instead.

properties.label: Links
properties.description: Directed energy-flow links (From feeds To). Allows multiple feeders per node and producer inputs.

properties.label: From
properties.description: Source node id — energy flows out of here.

properties.label: To
properties.description: Target node id — energy flows into here.

properties.label: AutoTags
properties.description: Tags for derived nodes (PDUs and outlets), which have no entry of their own to carry them. Matched by node id with '*' as a wildcard, e.g. 'outlet:rack_pdu_1:*'.

properties.label: Match
properties.description: Node id to match, with '*' matching any run of characters. e.g. 'outlet:rack_pdu_1:*' for every outlet on that PDU, 'pdu:*' for every PDU, or a single outlet's full id.

properties.label: Tags
properties.description: Tags to apply to every node the pattern matches. A tag never changes a reading — only what a view shows and what the exports may carry.

properties.label: Tags
properties.description: Tags declared up front, each with what it is for. Optional — a tag typed onto a node works without being declared. Declaring one lets it exist before anything carries it, and gives it a description.

properties.label: Name
properties.description: The tag itself, as it is written on a node, a rule or a destination filter.

properties.label: Description
properties.description: What this tag is for, in your own words. Shown wherever the tag is listed.

properties.label: Groups
properties.description: Named groups of nodes shown as one collapsible node on the flow graphs (e.g. three MPPTs as one 'Incoming PV'). Members keep their own links/exports; the group also exports its summed total.

properties.label: Id
properties.description: Stable unique id for the group (used in the group's exported topic/metric).

properties.label: Label
properties.description: Human-readable label shown on the flow diagram when the group is collapsed.

properties.label: Kind
properties.description: What the group represents, for diagram styling: 'node', 'panel', 'inverter', 'battery', 'solar', 'grid', or 'load'.

properties.label: Members
properties.description: The ids of the member nodes this group aggregates.

properties.label: Parents
properties.description: Legacy single-feeder map (child id -> parent id). Prefer Links; still honored for back-compat.

properties.label: InferFromConservation
properties.description: Work out an unmeasured node's value from what it feeds, when exactly one path could have supplied it. Sound arithmetic, but it describes the hierarchy you drew rather than anything measured — so results are always labelled 'inferred'. Turn it off to show 'no data' instead.

properties.label: MqttExport
properties.description: Publish each energy-hierarchy tier's rolled-up value to MQTT every poll.

properties.label: MqttExportTags
properties.description: Limit the MQTT export to nodes with particular tags. Empty exports every node. Filtering changes only what is sent — never a value, and never any other destination.

properties.label: Include
properties.description: Only send nodes carrying at least one of these tags. Empty sends every node.

properties.label: Exclude
properties.description: Never send nodes carrying any of these tags. Takes precedence over Include.

properties.label: MqttTopicTemplate
properties.description: Template for each tier's MQTT topic. Placeholders: {parent} (MQTT parent topic), {id}, {label}, {kind}, {metric}, {units}. e.g. '{parent}/energyflow/{id}'.

label: Modbus
description: Modbus TCP connections that energy-flow nodes can be bound to (inverters, meters, PLCs).

properties.label: Connections
properties.description: Modbus TCP devices to poll. Add one per device, then reference it from a source binding's Connection.

properties.label: Id
properties.description: Stable id used to reference this connection from a source binding.

properties.label: Name
properties.description: Friendly name for the device (shown in the editor).

properties.label: Host
properties.description: Hostname or IP address of the Modbus TCP device.

properties.label: Port
properties.description: TCP port the device listens on (Modbus TCP default 502; RS485-to-Ethernet gateways often use 4196, 8899, or 502).

properties.label: Framing
properties.description: Wire protocol: 'auto' (try native Modbus TCP, then Modbus RTU over TCP, and use whichever the device answers), 'tcp' (native Modbus TCP), or 'rtu-over-tcp' (Modbus RTU frames over a raw TCP socket — what most RS485-to-Ethernet gateways / serial dongles speak, e.g. an EG4 inverter on port 4196/8899). Leave on 'auto' unless you want to pin one.

properties.label: UnitId
properties.description: Modbus unit / slave id.

properties.label: PollIntervalSeconds
properties.description: How often to poll this device, in seconds.

properties.label: TimeoutMs
properties.description: Read/write timeout per Modbus request, in milliseconds. Lower it to fail faster on an unresponsive device; raise it for a slow gateway.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Poll this device. Turn off to disable it without deleting the connection.

label: Plugins
description: Settings for externally loaded plugins, keyed by plugin id.

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Use a Redis/Valkey instance for shared, durable state (today: the energy accumulator).

properties.label: Connection
properties.description: Redis/Valkey endpoint, host:port. A full StackExchange.Redis connection string also works, e.g. "valkey:6379,ssl=false".

properties.label: Password
properties.description: Password, if the instance requires one. Leave blank for an unauthenticated instance on a trusted network.

properties.label: KeyPrefix
properties.description: Prefix for every key written, so the instance can be shared with other applications.

properties.label: ConnectTimeoutSeconds
properties.description: Seconds to wait when connecting before falling back to local state.

label: Operator
description: Kubernetes operator: let this release manage its own Deployment (registry update checks, optional self-update).

properties.label: Enabled
properties.description: Enable the Kubernetes operator: let this release manage its own Deployment (registry update checks, optional self-update). Requires the Kubernetes config source and the 'operator' role. No effect otherwise.

properties.label: CheckForUpdates
properties.description: Periodically check the container registry for a newer image and report it (in the CR status and the GUI Diagnostics page). Read-only — never changes the Deployment on its own.

properties.label: CheckIntervalHours
properties.description: How often to check the registry for updates, in hours.

properties.label: Policy
properties.description: How far an update may move the deployed version: Patch (same major.minor), Minor (same major, no breaking changes), or Major (any newer release).

properties.label: AutoUpdate
properties.description: Automatically roll the Deployment to the newest eligible release (bounded by Policy). Off by default — checking is safe, but applying an update restarts the workload.

properties.label: Registry
properties.description: Override the registry host to query (e.g. ghcr.io). Defaults to the registry of the currently-deployed image.

properties.label: Repository
properties.description: Override the repository to query (e.g. xtremeownage/rpdu2mqtt). Defaults to the repository of the currently-deployed image.
